As a former career soldier in the People’s Liberation Army (pla), she does not naively revisit the imagery of the woman soldier so central to Communist revolutionary cultural production. She reinhabits a subjectivity that shaped her life and art in order to review it from the focus afforded by the optical device—the binoculars or camera—she raises to her eyes. With this pair of photographs and the continuation of her
series that followed, Lei Yan activates an image world of women viewing the world anew through binoculars, a complex network of images invoked in the process of looking and making.
zh: 一个身穿迷彩背心和迷彩裤的女人站在沼泽地上，双手举着望远镜贴在眼前。艺术家雷燕以这副模样出现在两幅一组的照片《如果长征是一场女权运动？》（图4.04）和《如果他们是女人？》（图4.05）中。这两幅照片是她为"长征"项目在泸沽湖与朱迪·芝加哥相遇而创作的。作为中国人民解放军（PLA）的一名退役职业军人，她并非天真地重访共产主义革命文化生产中如此核心的女兵形象。她重新栖居于一种塑造了她人生与艺术的主体性，以便从她举到眼前的视觉器具——望远镜或相机——所提供的焦点去审视它。通过这两幅照片以及随后延续的《如果》系列，雷燕激活了一个由举着望远镜重新观看世界的女性构成的图像世界，一个在观看与创作过程中被唤起的复杂图像网络。

en: A woman in a long black skirt and high-collared jacket stands at water’s edge. Strokes of green ink sprout around the hem of her skirt and weave through the pattern on her jacket. The blue of the bow in her hair echoes the gradations of wash tinting water, sky, and distant mountains. Three small sailboats cleave to and accentuate the horizon line. With her back to the viewer, the woman gazes through binoculars, not at the water, boats, or mountains, but upward toward a flying machine in the top right corner. The black-and-white form suggests an airplane, but closer inspection reveals a fantastical abstraction, an assemblage of crosshatched shapes. The wings are not flush with one another. A basket or a net hangs from the undercarriage, with a sandbaglike form dangling down. This illustration (figure 7.01) appeared on the October 1916 cover of

(Funü shibao), a journal published in Shanghai during the first six years of Republican-era China (1911–49). Its new woman on the verge of flight from earth into the heavens stands as one instance in a genealogy of women with binoculars to their eyes.
Twenty some years earlier, Wu Youru, a popular illustrator of urban vignettes for the pictorial supplement to Shanghai’s
newspaper, had depicted three courtesans on an upper balcony “sightseeing” with a pair of binoculars.

Framed by the balcony balustrade, they gaze out from an interior space, over the rooftops of neighboring buildings, toward something beyond the image’s edge. The woman holding the binoculars leans over, tilting her line of sight slightly downward. These elegantly attired “blossoms” of the pleasure quarter display not only their conspicuous consumption of modern technology, but also their visual mastery. They are caught, as they are looked at, in the act of looking. The world-making power of vision, outward and upward, symbolizes women’s move out of the “inner quarters” of traditional Chinese society.
zh: 一个身穿黑色长裙、高领上衣的女人站在水边。绿色墨迹从裙摆周围生出，穿行于她上衣的图案之间。她发间蝴蝶结的蓝色，与晕染水面、天空和远山的深浅墨色相互呼应。三只小帆船紧贴并凸显出地平线。女人背对观者，举着望远镜，看的不是水面、船只或群山，而是右上方一架飞行器。那黑白形体像是飞机，细看却是奇异的抽象构成，由一组交叉排线的形状拼合而成。两翼并不齐平，起落架下挂着一只篮子或一张网，还有一个沙袋状的东西垂下来。这幅插图（图7.01）刊于1916年10月《妇女时报》封面。该刊于民国（1911—1949）最初六年间在上海出版。那位即将从大地飞向天空的新女性，构成了"举着望远镜的女人"谱系中的一个实例。
二十多年前，为上海《申报》图画副刊绘制市井小品的著名画家吴友如，曾描绘过三名妓女站在楼上阳台上，举着一副望远镜"看风景"。
她们被阳台栏杆框住，从室内空间向外望去，越过邻近建筑的屋顶，看向图像边缘之外的某物。举望远镜的女子俯身向前，视线微微下倾。这些衣饰优雅的风月场的"花朵"，不仅展示着对现代技术的炫耀性消费，也展示着视觉上的掌控力。她们在被观看的同时，也被捕捉于观看的动作之中。向外、向上的视觉所具有的世界营造之力，象征着女性走出传统中国社会的"内闱"。

en: During the New Culture movement of the early Republican period, the “woman question” preoccupied reformers in their quest to overturn China’s feudal and colonial history. They saw women as central to the project of modernity, even as they debated how to liberate women and what their role in the new nation would be. Reform efforts simultaneously gave rise to a literary revolution, as authors began to use

, or vernacular, instead of classical Chinese, which for centuries had preserved literacy as an elite domain. Popular newspapers and magazines flooded the urban market, creating a new reading public. Women became a target audience, and while nationalists discussed the “woman question” often through their desire as humiliated male colonial subjects to emerge on the world stage, female readers and writers articulated their thoughts and stories in these new publications.
The illustration on the October 1916 cover of

presents this aspiring female subject with her power of vision and dreams of flight. Two articles within narrate the heroism of Zhang Xiahun, a young woman who, on attending a Shanghai air show, insisted on flying. She ignored the head of the aviation school, who tried to dissuade her, and proclaimed her flight would “open a new era of Chinese women pilots, forge a new dawn in the history of female bravery, and merit several lines in China’s aviation history.”

When a strong wind arose and caused the plane to crash, she walked away injured but triumphant. This new woman, binoculars aimed toward the horizon, haunts the pair of photographs Lei Yan created almost a century later for
. Garbed now in camouflage and black military boots, she stands her ground not on a balcony or at water’s edge but on the battlefield of history.
zh: 在民国初年的新文化运动中，"妇女问题"成为改革者力图推翻中国封建与殖民历史的核心关切。他们将女性视为现代性工程的核心，同时也在争论如何解放妇女、妇女在新国家中应扮演何种角色。改革同时催生了一场文学革命：作者们开始使用白话而非文言，而文言几个世纪以来一直使识字成为精英的专属领域。通俗报刊与杂志大量涌入城市市场，造就了新的阅读公众。女性成为目标读者；民族主义者讨论"妇女问题"，往往出于身为受辱的男性殖民臣民、渴望登上世界舞台的欲望，而女性读者与作者则在这些新出版物中表述自己的思想与故事。
《妇女时报》1916年10月号的封面插图，呈现的正是这样一位怀抱视觉之力与飞行之梦、心向高处的女性主体。同期两篇文章讲述了年轻女子 Zhang Xiahun 的英勇事迹：她参观上海一场飞行表演时，坚持要乘坐飞机。她不顾航空学校校长的劝阻，宣称自己的飞行将"开辟中国女飞行员的新纪元，为女性勇敢史缔造新的黎明，并在中国航空史上赢得数行记载"。
一阵强风刮来，飞机坠毁；她受伤脱身，却带着胜利者的姿态。这位把望远镜对准地平线的新女性，幽灵般萦绕着雷燕近一个世纪后为"长征"创作的那两幅照片。如今她一身迷彩、脚蹬黑色军靴，不再站在阳台或水边，而是坚守在历史的战场上。

en: Lei Yan’s

series inspired the conception of feminist sight lines that frames this final section of the book. I interpret her work as feminist because of its critical historiographical consciousness cultivated by being on the periphery. I met Lei Yan, as described in chapter 4, not in Beijing but in rural Yunnan, albeit through an art exhibit organized in and emanating from the “cultural capital” of Beijing. She works primarily in Kunming but trained in the pla Arts Academy in Beijing and continues to exhibit her work there. Her center-off-center position, as well as the conjunction of the turning point of her career after retirement from the military with that of Chinese contemporary art production, informs the transhistorical and transnational connections her artwork makes visible. The feminist sight lines opened by her evolving body of work provide a critical vantage on the work of art in the era of late socialism-late liberalism, as these two social projects and their management of difference and inequality intertwine. When she and Ai Weiwei both responded through their art to state image control of the 2008 Wenquan earthquake, she entered into relational monumental/ephemeral proximity with China’s most globally recognized art world figure. Viewed together, the questions Lei’s work raises about conventional narratives of Chinese contemporary art emerge in particular relief.
zh: 雷燕的《如果》系列启发了本书最后一部分用以统摄全局的"女性主义视线"概念。我之所以将她的作品解读为女性主义的，是因为它带有一种由边缘位置培养出来的批判性史学意识。如第四章所述，我与雷燕相遇不在北京，而是在云南乡间，尽管那是通过一场在北京"文化首都"中组织并向外辐射的艺术展览。她主要在昆明工作，却曾在北京的解放军艺术学院受训，并继续在那里展出作品。她偏离中心的中心位置，以及她退役后艺术生涯的转折点与中国当代艺术生产的转折点相合，都塑造了她的作品所揭示的跨历史、跨国联系。她不断演化的作品所开启的女性主义视线，为审视晚期社会主义—晚期自由主义时代的艺术提供了一个批判性视点，因为这两种社会工程及其对差异与不平等的管理正相互交织。当她与艾未未都以艺术回应国家对2008年汶川地震图像的控制时，她与中国最受全球瞩目的艺术界人物进入了纪念碑式／短暂性的关系性邻近之中。将两人的作品并置来看，雷燕作品对当代中国艺术常规叙事提出的问题便格外清晰地显现出来。

en: Feminist Sight Lines
zh: 女性主义视线

en: Binoculars bring something distant into closer view. Side-mounted mirror-symmetrical telescopes, designed to be hand held, produce an impression of depth that makes the scene viewed three-dimensional. When Lei Yan shows up in her stereoscopelike images

en: ?, she reverses the sight line of her historical counterparts from the previous turn of the century. The courtesan as public figure of urbanity and the learned new woman of the Republic gaze toward an imagined future, what once seemed impossibly distant suddenly brought near. In 2002, Lei trains her binoculars back on a Communist past meant to seem distant in reform-era discourse about linking tracks with the capitalist world. Instead, she brings it near, as historical figures from 1934 loom large on the horizon.
zh: 望远镜能把远处之物拉近。两侧镜像对称、可手持的望远镜产生景深，使所观景物显得立体。当雷燕以她那两幅立体镜式的照片《如果长征是一场女权运动？》和《如果他们是女人？》现身时，她颠倒了上一个世纪之交与她遥相呼应的那些女性的视线。作为城市性公共形象的妓女，与民国博学的新女性，都凝望着一个想象出来的未来——那曾显得遥不可及的一切，忽然被拉到了近前。2002年，雷燕把望远镜调转，回望一段在改革时代关于与世界资本主义接轨的话语中被刻意显得遥远的共产主义过去。她反而把它拉近，让1934年的历史人物赫然矗立在地平线上。

en: The feminist grammar of her “what if” titles is akin to that of the future anterior employed by Tani Barlow in her reading of Ding Ling’s Maoist literary corpus. Barlow argues that the revolutionary injunction for cultural workers like Ding to “enter life” (

) meant more than living with and representing the common people. It expressed a Maoist cultural idiolect that invented language for mass consciousness and action on the historical horizon, a dialectical process of “anticipate, initiate, reflect, criticize, regroup, and reanticipate.”

As Ding entered life in this sense, her stories and novels not only reflected this process, they became part of the process, even while holding on to the speculative question about what “women” would become through their enunciation as such. The future anterior guides the historian to focus on theoretical claims from the past about the potential women were imagined to embody. Barlow uses this grammatical construction as a methodology for reassessing not only the legacy of Chinese feminism but of feminism as an international mode of thought linked to colonialism and globalization, as much a measure of one’s place in the world order as a demand for liberation. The future anterior makes possible a speculative question: What will women have been? It does not presume to know what the “woman” predicated by feminism existentially is or was but endeavors to understand how the category of woman has been mobilized toward future change of an untenable status quo.
The artworks produced by Lei Yan through her participation in

raise related questions about what women might have become if they had not been caught by the double binds of Chinese Communist history. She roams back and forth over this and more recent historical terrain, performing an auto-ethnographic excavation of the institutions and socio-historical processes that made her as both artist and woman.
zh: 她那些"如果"标题的女性主义语法，近似于白露（Tani Barlow）在解读丁玲毛泽东时代文学文本时所用的"将来完成时"。白露认为，对丁玲这样的文化工作者发出的"深入生活"的革命号召，并不只是与群众共同生活并表现他们。它表达的是一种毛泽东时代的文化独特语汇，为历史地平线上的群众意识与行动发明语言，是一个"预判、倡导、反映、批评、重组、再预判"的辩证过程。

当丁玲以这种方式进入生活时，她的小说和故事不仅反映了这一过程，也成为过程的一部分，同时还保留着一个思辨性问题："妇女"通过被如此言说将会变成什么。将来完成时引导历史学者关注过去的理论主张——关于女性被想象可以承载的潜能。白露用这一语法结构作为一种方法，不仅重新评估中国女性主义的遗产，也重新评估女性主义作为一种与殖民主义和全球化相连的国际思想方式；它既是衡量一个人在世界秩序中所处位置的尺度，也是对解放的要求。将来完成时使一个思辨性问题成为可能：女性将会曾经成为什么？它并不自以为知道女性主义所断定的"女人"在存在论上是什么或曾是什么，而是努力理解"女人"这一范畴如何被动员起来，以推动对一个难以维持的现状的未来改变。
雷燕通过参与"长征"创作的作品，提出了相关问题：如果女性没有被中国共产党历史的双重束缚所捕获，她们可能会成为什么？她在这片历史地形与更晚近的历史地形之间来回漫游，对自己既成为艺术家又成为女人所凭借的建制与社会历史过程，进行了一场自我民族志式的挖掘。

en: Lei Yan’s trajectory as an artist began with a career in the Chinese military that spanned three decades. Born into a Kunming military family in 1957, she joined the army at age fourteen and served over the years as a soldier, nurse, and officer. As part of her early duties, she gained sketching skills and responsibility for drawing her unit’s blackboard announcements. In 1976, she began studying printmaking. She also transferred to the Kunming Military District Creative Works Team and had her work shown in China’s National Military Art Exhibition. With her next assignment to a local military hospital, she became an official painter tasked with illustrating teaching materials for the military medical school. After “reform and opening,” the school opened a multimedia lab, where she studied color photography. She also served, as a nurse, during the prolonged border conflicts of the Sino-Vietnamese War. In 1989, she tested into the first printmaking course offered by the People’s Liberation Army Arts Academy in Beijing and arrived in the capital shortly after the

exhibit at the National Art Museum of China brought new attention and notoriety to contemporary practices such as installation and performance art. After graduating in 1991, she returned to Kunming and experimented, outside her official capacity, with new styles and subject matter. She joined a group of artists working in Kunming’s Chuang Ku, or Loft community, established in a former factory, where she set up a studio after her retirement from the military in 2001.
After she and fellow Kunming-based artist Sun Guojuan joined Judy Chicago at site six of

, they participated in cross-cultural art exchanges to Sweden facilitated by TGC Nordica, a Chinese-Swedish organization that opened a gallery space in the Kunming Loft complex in 2000. Through this gallery, Lei and Sun curated a series of exhibitions featuring the work of female artists from Yunnan.
zh: 雷燕的艺术生涯始于在中国军队中度过的三十年。她1957年出生于昆明的一个军人家庭，十四岁入伍，此后多年先后当过士兵、护士和军官。早年职责之一，是学习素描，并负责绘制部队的黑板报。1976年，她开始学习版画。她后来调入昆明军区创作组，作品入选全军美术作品展。下一次被分配到当地一所军医院后，她成为专职画家，负责为军医学校的教学材料绘制插图。改革开放后，学校开设多媒体实验室，她在那里学习彩色摄影。在中越战争漫长的边境冲突中，她还担任过护士。1989年，她考取解放军艺术学院在北京开设的第一届版画课程，并在"中国现代艺术展"于中国美术馆举办、使装置和行为艺术等当代实践引起新的关注与争议后不久抵达首都。1991年毕业后，她回到昆明，在官方职责之外尝试新的风格与题材。她加入了在昆明"创库"（由一家旧工厂改建的艺术家社区）工作的艺术家群体，并于2001年退役后在那里设立工作室。
她与同在昆明的艺术家孙国娟一起在"长征"第六站与朱迪·芝加哥会合后，又参加了由 TGC Nordica 促成的赴瑞典跨文化艺术交流。这家中国—瑞典机构于2000年在昆明创库开设画廊。通过这家画廊，雷燕与孙国娟策划了一系列展览，呈现云南女性艺术家的作品。

en: Lei Yan is not particularly well known outside of minor transnational networks linking, for example, Yunnan with Scandinavia. Nor is her path to becoming an artist via the military one typically associated with contemporary art practice, especially that in an avant-garde, anti-institutional mode, although it does bring back into the picture the longer translingual history of avant-garde/

in China. It is precisely this center-off-center position that informs her work. The pieces she began creating after her retirement exemplify a critical historiographical consciousness, a feminist reflection on past avant-gardes that temporally confounds the straight logic of innovation, progress, and coming before. She works from within a national representational corpus, subjecting it to various experiments informed by transnational art movements, to reveal the fields of violence—literal and figural—it has enacted. She is a propagandist turned deconstructionist, with a vision in which the
relations between man and woman inform other socially reproduced abstractions—past and present, rural and urban, China and the world—that create injustice.
zh: 雷燕在连接云南与斯堪的纳维亚等地的小型跨国网络之外并不特别知名。她经由军队成为艺术家的道路，通常也不被与当代艺术实践联系在一起——尤其是那种先锋、反建制的实践——尽管它确实把中国"先锋"（xianfeng）更长时段的跨语言历史重新带回了画面。正是这种偏离中心的中心位置，塑造了她的作品。退役后开始创作的作品体现出批判性的史学意识，一种对过往先锋派的女性主义反思，在时间上扰乱了创新、进步、先行的直线逻辑。她从一套国家表征语汇内部工作，让它经受各种受跨国艺术运动启发的实验，从而揭示它曾施行的暴力场域——字面的与比喻的。她是从宣传家转变为解构者的人，在她的视野中，男女（nannü）关系塑造着其他由社会再生产出来的抽象对立——过去与现在、乡村与城市、中国与世界——并制造不公。

en: Three sociohistorical categories—the woman soldier, the military artist, and the woman artist—have shaped Lei Yan’s life and art. The ways they intersect throw into question conventional narratives of feminist art in global and national contexts. Her career does not, for example, fit easily into the story of feminist art emerging from 1960s Euro-American Second Wave feminist critiques of the art world and its social and formalistic hierarchies. It similarly resists Chinese articulations of

as a post-socialist recuperation of female subjectivity that domesticates and depoliticizes work by women and thereby cuts it off from interpretation within larger contexts of the nation and beyond. Lei Yan’s artistic practice, its subject matter and formal aesthetics, requires consideration beyond the borders of the nation because of its critique of loss and sacrifice in the name of the nation. She arguably becomes a feminist artist in spite of or because of her original training as an artist in what is arguably the sine qua non of the modern Chinese nation-state, the People’s Liberation Army of the Chinese Communist Party.
zh: 女兵、军旅艺术家和女性艺术家这三个社会历史范畴，塑造了雷燕的人生与艺术。它们相互交汇的方式，使全球与民族语境中女性主义艺术的常规叙事受到质疑。例如，她的职业生涯不易被纳入这样一个故事：女性主义艺术诞生于1960年代欧美第二波女性主义对艺术界及其社会与形式等级所进行的批判。她的职业生涯同样难以纳入中国对"女性艺术"（nüxing yishu）的表述——那种把女性艺术当作后社会主义对女性主体性的收复，驯化并去政治化女性创作，从而使女性作品无法在民族国家内部及更大语境中被解读。雷燕的艺术实践、题材与形式美学，要求超越民族国家边界来考察，因为它批判以民族之名造成的丧失与牺牲。可以说，她成为女性主义艺术家，或是突破了最初的艺术训练所设下的限制，或恰恰得益于这种训练；训练她的机构是中国共产党领导的中国人民解放军，而这一机构可谓现代中国民族国家不可或缺的条件。

en: The categories of woman soldier (
), military artist (
), and woman artist (
) are historical catachreses, master words whose appearance in speech mark a departure from traditional usage (i.e., woman, soldier, artist) and serve to consolidate new social formations. In

children: The Question of Women in Chinese Feminism

en: , Tani Barlow argues that “woman” as expressed in the Chinese neologisms of
and

emerged as a theoretical category, rather than a universal given, out of the Chinese drive to form a modern nation. These historical catachreses and their analogues of nübing, junyi, and nüxing yishujia are ideological entities with explanatory power that over time served to organize everyday thinking.
zh: 女兵（nübing）、军旅艺术家（junyi）和女性艺术家（nüxing yishujia）这些范畴是历史性的词语误用，是主导词；它们在言语中的出现标志着对传统用法（即女人、士兵、艺术家）的偏离，并有助于巩固新的社会构形。在《中国女性主义中的女性问题》中，白露认为，"女性"与"妇女"这些中文新词所表达的"女人"，是在中国建设现代民族国家的驱动下作为理论范畴而非普遍给定物出现的。这些历史性的词语误用，以及女兵、军艺、女性艺术家等对应词，都是具有解释力的意识形态实体，在历史中逐渐组织起日常思维。

en: Beginning in the 1920s, the woman soldier in China signified a new subject, a woman liberated from traditional kinship protocols and empowered to fight for the idea of a new nation, free from feudal rule and its patriarchal oppressions, as well as colonial incursion and orientalist depictions of Asian women oppressed by their “culture” as justification for invasion. Xie Bingying served as one early model of this emerging subject. Born in 1906, she struggled to get an education, escaped from an arranged marriage, moved in and had a child with her lover, and served in the National Revolutionary Army in the fight against local warlords in the 1920s and the Japanese in the 1930s. The publication of her war diaries, first in 1928, followed by updated versions, made her story available for wide public consumption.

In breathless prose, she wrote, for example, of her first night after joining the female company of Wuhan’s Central Military and Political School: “I thought how in only a few hours we would be carrying guns and sticks, marching to the cry of ‘one-two-three-four.’

. What a powerful word! I would not have believed that we Chinese women, repressed by ancient custom for thousands of years, would see the day when we would become soldiers. Now we must work hard to carry out our responsibility, to change society, to destroy the powers of feudalism.”
The woman soldier, glorified in films such as

(1970), became a key figure in the Chinese Communist Party’s pantheon of heroic representation. The woman soldier and her visibility in film, propaganda posters, and painting supported party rhetoric about female emancipation and gender equality. She also provided women with a new subject position, a potentiality some embraced, even as they continued to encounter gender hierarchy and sexual violence in the military and elsewhere.
zh: 从1920年代开始，中国的女兵意味着一种新的主体，一个从传统亲属礼法中解放出来、被赋权为建立一个新国家的理念而战的女人，她既摆脱封建统治及其父权压迫，也对抗殖民入侵以及东方主义将亚洲女性描绘为受其"文化"压迫、从而为侵略辩护的做法。谢冰莹是这一新兴主体的早期典范之一。她1906年出生，为受教育而挣扎，逃离包办婚姻，与恋人同居并育有一个孩子，1920年代在国民革命军中参加讨伐地方军阀的战斗，1930年代又投身抗日。她的战地日记于1928年首次出版，此后又出过增订版，使她的故事得以广泛流传。
她用令人屏息的文字写道，例如，加入武汉中央军事政治学校女生队后的第一夜："我想着，再过几个小时，我们就要扛起枪和棍棒，随着'一二三四'的口令行进。士兵。多么有力的词！我简直无法相信，我们中国女性被古老礼俗压抑了数千年，竟能活着看到成为士兵的一天。现在我们一定要努力履行自己的责任，改变社会，摧毁封建势力。"
女兵在《中华女儿》（1949）、《红色娘子军》（1961）和《红灯记》（1970）等影片中被颂扬，成为中国共产党英雄表征殿堂中的关键形象。女兵及其在电影、宣传画和绘画中的可见性，支撑着党关于妇女解放与性别平等的修辞。她也为女性提供了一个新的主体位置，一种有些人欣然拥抱的可能性，尽管她们在军队内外仍不断遭遇性别等级与性暴力。

en: The modern conception of the military artist or art soldier dates to the Red Army’s establishment of its guerrilla base in Yan’an, where Mao Zedong compelled culture workers to become willing oxen, heads bowed to serve the people. His selective quotation from Lu Xun’s poem “Self Mockery” as final salvo in his talks on literature and art draws power from Lu’s conviction that only culture could save China from the habits of thought and behavior that had made it weak. Mao’s didactic interpretation of the quoted couplet, however, disregards ironic contrasts in the full poem, whose narrator reflects on the defiant gestures of his past and ends with a desire to retreat from the outside world to “a small house hidden away.”

Mao emphasized cultural defiance, reformulation, and revolutionary anticipation over contemplative ambivalence, clearing the ground for ccp institutionalization of culture workers and performance troops. The Yan’an Lu Xun Arts Academy was established in 1938, two years after the death of its namesake.

As part of this institutional legacy, the People’s Liberation Army Arts Academy, established in Beijing in 1960, began offering advanced training for members of military cultural troops in art, dance, drama, literature, and music. Culture as the front line continued during the Cultural Revolution in Red Guard art activities such as the 1967

children: Long Live the Victory of Chairman Mao’s Revolutionary Line

en: exhibit at the National Art Museum of China.
Ballet, film, and opera productions like
effectively fused together the figures of woman soldier and military artist.
zh: 军旅艺术家或艺术战士的现代观念，可追溯到红军在延安建立游击根据地时期。毛泽东迫使文化工作者做甘愿俯首为人民服务的牛。他在文艺讲话结尾选择性引用鲁迅《自嘲》中的诗句，其力量来自鲁迅的信念：只有文化才能把中国从使其积弱的思维与行为习惯中拯救出来。然而，毛泽东对所引诗句的说教式解释，无视整首诗中的反讽对照；诗中的叙述者回望自己昔日的桀骜姿态，最后却渴望从外部世界退隐到"躲进小楼"。
毛泽东强调文化上的反抗、重新表述与革命预判，而非沉思性的矛盾心理，从而为中国共产党将文化工作者和演出队伍建制化扫清道路。延安鲁迅艺术学院成立于1938年，即其命名对象去世两年之后。
作为这一制度遗产的一部分，1960年在北京成立的解放军艺术学院开始为军队文艺团体的成员提供美术、舞蹈、戏剧、文学和音乐方面的高级培训。文化作为前线，在文化大革命期间的红卫兵美术活动中延续，例如1967年在中国美术馆举办的"毛主席革命路线胜利万岁"展览。
芭蕾、电影和歌剧作品如《红色娘子军》，有效地把女兵与军旅艺术家的形象熔合在一起。

en: The idea of the woman artist arose in a post-Mao context, as the Chinese art historical category of nüxing yishu gained currency in the 1990s, casting a retrospective net that pulled modernist figures into its project. It emerged in exhibit catalogues and art criticism in 1995, the year Beijing hosted the United Nations Fourth World Conference on Women, and then served as the organizing rubric for the

exhibit at the National Art Museum of China in 1998. Following the centennial frame of the exhibit’s title, catalogue essays on early twentieth-century painters such as Pan Yuliang and Qiu Ti discussed them as predecessors of a “women’s art” shaped by women’s unique psychobiological predispositions. This discursive formation, as part of post-Mao feminist humanist thought that sought to recuperate a female subjectivity from the state mobilization of women, identifies a subject different from that signified by female artist (
), or artist who happens to be a woman. The curator of

, Jia Fangzhou, defined in his catalogue introduction the main characteristics of this art: it draws inspiration from personal reflection and experience, demonstrates “artistic intuition,” breaks from rational thought, focuses on the minutiae of daily life rather than politics, and develops both material and method from “handicrafts” associated with women.
Two years later, in

children: A History of Chinese Contemporary Art, 1990–1999

en: , one of the first comprehensive surveys of this period, Chinese art historian Lü Peng relegated almost all female artists to a chapter titled “Women’s Art,” rather than as contributors to movements discussed in other chapters, such as political pop, cynical realism, or conceptual art.
zh: 女性艺术家的观念兴起于后毛泽东时代。中文艺术史范畴"女性艺术"在1990年代流行开来，回溯性地张开一张网，把现代主义人物也拉进其计划。它于1995年出现在展览图录和艺术批评中——那一年北京主办了联合国第四次世界妇女大会——随后成为1998年中国美术馆"世纪·女性"展览的组织标题。依照展览标题的百年框架，图录中讨论潘玉良、丘堤等20世纪初画家的文章，把她们视为一种"女性艺术"的先驱；这种艺术由女性独特的心理生物学禀赋所塑造。这一话语构形是后毛泽东时代女性主义人道主义思想的产物，它试图从国家对妇女的动员中收复女性主体性，并标示出一种不同于"女艺术家"（nü yishujia，即碰巧是女人的艺术家）的主体。展览"世纪·女性"的策展人贾方舟在图录导言中界定了这种艺术的主要特征：它从个人反思与经验中汲取灵感，展现"艺术直觉"，与理性思维断裂，关注日常生活的细枝末节而非政治，并从与女性相关的"手工艺"中发展出材料与方法。
两年后，在中国艺术史学者吕澎所著的、这一时期的首批综合概览之一《中国当代艺术史：1990—1999》中，几乎所有女性艺术家都被归入题为"女性艺术"的一章，而不是作为政治波普、玩世现实主义或观念艺术等其他章节所讨论运动的参与者。

en: In 2002, Lei Yan brought the three ideological categories of woman soldier, military artist, and woman artist together in

children: What If the Long March Had Been a Women’s Rights Movement

en: ? and

children: What If They Had Been Women

en: ?, exhibited in the “women’s art” section of

project. While she created these images in response to Judy Chicago’s fantasy “what if” projection, her visual materials reference not a universal female subject but a formative Chinese historical event, as Communist activists regrouped in order to revolutionize a rural peasantry. Their appeal to disenfranchised men, “bare sticks” without the means to marry, held out the promise of equal opportunity to carry on one’s patriline rather than women’s liberation from the inner quarters of family life. Red Army guerrilla activities gradually prioritized class over gender in a way that suppressed thinking about class and gender as interlocking or mutually constitutive systems of power, even as representations of women raped and exploited by class enemies served a prominent symbolic function.

This ideological suppression produced the double binds at Yan’an that Ding Ling exposed so trenchantly in “Thoughts on March 8”: female comrades were denounced for pursuing politics over family responsibilities, but then when compelled to marry and bear children, they were denounced for being “Noras returned home,” unable to survive independently and thus consigned to a destiny of “backwardness.”

“It would be better,” she wrote before being attacked as “narrowly feminist,” “if there were less empty theorizing and more talk about real problems, so that theory and practice would not be divorced, and better if all Communist Party members were more responsible for their own moral conduct.”
An investigation of this relationship between theory and practice, between ideology and image making became part of Lei’s emerging praxis.
zh: 2002年，雷燕把女兵、军旅艺术家和女性艺术家这三个意识形态范畴汇聚于《如果长征是一场女权运动？》和《如果他们是女人？》中，并在"长征"项目的"女性艺术"部分展出。尽管她是为了回应朱迪·芝加哥幻想式的"如果"投射而创作这些图像，她的视觉材料所指涉的并不是普遍的女性主体，而是一个塑造现代中国的历史事件：共产党活动分子重新集结，以便在农村发动农民革命。他们对被剥夺权利的男性——无力娶妻的"光棍"——的号召，许诺的是延续父系血脉的平等机会，而不是把妇女从家庭生活的内闱中解放出来。红军游击活动逐渐把阶级置于性别之上，从而压抑了把阶级与性别视为相互扣连、相互构成的权力体系来思考，尽管阶级敌人强奸和剥削妇女的表征仍发挥着突出的象征功能。
这种意识形态压抑在延安造成了丁玲在《三八节有感》中尖锐揭示的双重束缚：女同志因追求政治而置家庭责任于不顾遭到谴责，可当她们被迫结婚生育后，又被斥为"回家的娜拉"，无法独立生存，从而被判定为"落后"。
"与其空谈理论，不如多谈实际问题，使理论与实践不致脱节；"她在被攻击为"狭隘女性主义"之前写道，"如果所有共产党员都能对自己的道德行为更负起责任，那就更好了。"
对这种理论与实践、意识形态与图像生产之间关系的探究，成为雷燕逐渐形成的实践的一部分。

en: Lei Yan first developed her technique of digital manipulation as a military artist. In 1994, she and colleague Tang Zhigang produced a photograph of military heroes titled
(figure 7.02), with the handwritten inscription of “A Souvenir of the People’s Photo Studio Serving the People.”

The layers of translucent color applied to the soldiers’ hands and faces accentuate the montage construction of the photograph, as it brings together, in the Maoist tradition of reworked historical images, a group of heroes in the impossible reality of a studio shot. The washed out national colors of red and yellow that shade their skin mimic old hand-colored photographs, tingeing the image with nostalgia and parody. In her 2002
photos, Lei reproduces this technique but also inserts herself, as part of the represented collectivity

distantiated creator-observer of its power. She becomes a frontline observer from the future within the historical photograph, who brings into focus an oppositional consciousness, posing historiographical questions about her own social formation.
zh: 雷燕首次发展出数码处理技术，是在她做军旅艺术家期间。1994年，她与同事唐志冈制作了一张题为《一个时代的合影》的军人英雄照片（图7.02），上面有手写题字"为人民服务的人民照相馆留念"。

敷在士兵手和脸上的半透明色层，突出了照片的蒙太奇构造：它延续毛泽东时代改写历史图像的传统，把一群英雄聚合进照相馆合影这一不可能的现实之中。晕染他们皮肤的红黄两种国家象征色因褪色而显得暗淡，模仿着手工上色的老照片，为图像染上怀旧与戏仿的色调。在2002年的《如果》照片中，雷燕复制了这种技术，同时也把自己插入其中：她既是被再现的集体的一部分，又是对其力量保持距离的创作者—观察者。她成为历史照片中来自未来的前线观察者，把一个对抗性的意识带入焦点，并对自身的社会构形提出史学问题。

en: She continued the series with several more pieces.

children: What If Our Factory Were Still Here

en: ? (figure 7.03) emerged from video and photographic documentation of a factory within her military work unit as it underwent demolition. Like other artists who focused on the massing turning over of China’s urban landscape, Lei used her camera to explore sites of physical change. Her images bring to this presentist form of documentation questions of temporality, history, and memory. She inserts herself again within the frame, but this time the figure seems more a camouflaged observer from the past in panoramic projects of future destruction. Her image of the factory, an institutional space that once organized and defined social life, is imbued with a sense of loss: through the question she asks of it, her use of the possessive pronoun “our,” and her digitally manipulated spectral appearance within it. She stands in miniature with her binoculars, amid the rubble, witness to the dismantling of the political fervor and everyday activity that once filled the now empty space. The military as a site of female opportunity, talent development, and collectivity, as well as oppression, is demolished in the push toward market reform, demobilization, and privatization.
zh: 她继续创作这个系列，又增添了几件作品。《如果我们的工厂还在？》（图7.03）源于她对自己军队工作单位内一座工厂拆除过程的录像与摄影记录。与其他关注中国城市地貌大规模翻建的艺术家一样，雷燕用相机探索物质变迁的场所。她的图像为这种当下主义的记录方式带来了时间性、历史与记忆的问题。她再次把自己放入画面，但这一次，她更像未来毁灭全景图中的一名来自过去的迷彩观察者。她镜头下的工厂——一个曾经组织和界定社会生活的机构空间——弥漫着失落感：这来自她向它提出的问题，来自所有格"我们的"，也来自她经过数码处理的幽灵般现身。她以微缩身形举着望远镜站在瓦砾之间，见证着曾经充满这片如今空荡空间的政治热情与日常活动被拆解。军队作为女性获得机会、发展才能和集体归属之地，同时也是压迫之地，在市场化改革、裁军与私有化的推进中被拆除。

What If Woman Were Written by the Book

en: ? shifts to a sociological investigation of reform-era femininity produced out of and against previous norms, retrospectively framed as having unnaturally suppressed an essential femininity. For this piece, Lei Yan photographed the covers of popular books for sale on the streets of Kunming with titles containing the word “woman.” An inordinate number of them addressed issues related to health, beauty, sexuality, and family, positioning women as consumers of domestic pleasures rather than producers in the public sphere. She digitally montaged them together to form a black-and-white mosaic, over which the English word

in capital letters floats as a layered mask that reveals the gaudy colors of the book covers below. The question of the piece’s title suggests the disciplining of woman into a particular subject position by this proliferating abundance of material on her, while also holding open in its grammatical construction a gap between signifier and signified, in which the signifiers do not wholly make the signified in its image.
zh: 《如果女人按书本来塑造？》转向对改革时代女性气质的社会学考察：这种女性气质是在先前规范之内并针对先前规范生产出来的，而那些规范又被回溯性地框定为曾不自然地压抑了一种本质性的女性气质。为此，雷燕拍摄了昆明街头出售的畅销书封面，书名中都含有"女人"一词。其中相当多涉及健康、美貌、性与家庭，把女性定位为家庭乐趣的消费者，而非公共领域中的生产者。她用数码技术把它们蒙太奇式地拼成黑白马赛克，上面浮着大写的英文单词 woman，像一层叠置的面具，透出下方书封艳俗的色彩。作品标题的疑问暗示：铺天盖地、不断增殖的关于女人的材料，正把女人规训进特定的主体位置；而标题的语法构造同时保持着能指与所指之间的缝隙——能指并不能在其形象中完全制造所指。

en: In 2002, following her

children: Bullet Shot through a Young Heart

en: after a return trip to Laoshan, where she had served as a military nurse during the Sino-Vietnamese War. This prolonged series of conflicts along China’s border with Vietnam began with a bloody month in 1979 that left tens of thousands on both sides dead and injured. The war pitted, in almost a 180-degree turn, former socialist allies against one another. Cold War geopolitical alignments and the ideological battles of the Sino-Soviet split begun in the 1960s played out in deadly ways for Chinese and Vietnamese soldiers and civilians. After the Communist victory of the Viet Cong in 1975, a postcolonial, pro-Soviet regime was established in Vietnam. In neighboring Cambodia, the Chinese backed the Khmer Rouge. When their troops attacked ethnic Vietnamese in Cambodia and threatened the border, Vietnam counterattacked in a conflict that led to the deposing of Maoist client-leader Pol Pot. The Chinese retaliated with the 1979 invasion that launched the Sino-Vietnamese War. Border skirmishes continued throughout the 1980s until relations between the two countries finally normalized in the early 1990s. A devastating battle occurred at Laoshan in 1984, during Lei Yan’s deployment, and 959 Chinese soldiers and support personnel were buried there in the Malipo Martyrs Cemetery. Tombstone inscriptions indicate that many of those buried had enlisted only months before dying young, between the ages of sixteen and twenty. Upon returning to Laoshan almost twenty years later, Lei Yan noted that the rebranding of the area as a vacation destination remained haunted by Malipo: “I climbed to the top of the cemetery. Backlit, the tombstones appeared like a group of soldiers in uniform. A gust of wind swept by, and a chill struck through me, like a bullet shot through the tombstones and the spirits underneath. It shot through my young heart, through time and space, through memory, and through peace.”
zh: 2002年，完成《如果》系列之后，雷燕重返老山，随后创作了另一件数码摄影作品《子弹穿过年轻的心》。她曾在中越战争期间作为军队护士驻守老山。中国与越南边境上这场旷日持久的冲突系列，始于1979年血腥的一个月，双方数万人死伤。战争几乎来了个一百八十度大转弯，让昔日的社会主义盟友兵戎相见。冷战地缘政治格局与1960年代开始的中苏分裂意识形态斗争，以致命的方式落在中国和越南的士兵与平民身上。1975年越共取得胜利后，越南建立起一个后殖民、亲苏的政权。在邻国柬埔寨，中国支持红色高棉。当红色高棉军队袭击柬埔寨境内的越南族并威胁边境时，越南反击，冲突导致受毛主义阵营扶植的领导人波尔布特被推翻。中国以1979年的入侵进行报复，中越战争由此爆发。边境冲突贯穿整个1980年代，直到1990年代初两国关系最终正常化。1984年，雷燕驻防期间，老山发生了一场毁灭性的战斗，959名中国士兵和支援人员葬于麻栗坡烈士陵园。墓碑铭文显示，许多死者入伍仅数月便阵亡，年仅十六到二十岁。近二十年后重返老山时，雷燕注意到，该地区被重新包装为度假目的地，却仍被麻栗坡的幽灵萦绕："我爬到了陵园顶上。逆光中，墓碑看上去像一队身着军装的士兵。一阵风扫过，寒意刺透了我，像一颗子弹穿过墓碑和下面的亡灵。它穿过我年轻的心，穿过时间和空间，穿过记忆，也穿过和平。"

en: (figure 7.04) is a triptych of three photographs, each tinted a single color, which hung side by side resemble the bars of an exploded national flag. In the central, black-and-white image, superimposed layers of tombstones crowd the frame. While the Malipo tombstones are uniform in height and shape and laid out in straight, uniform rows, Lei digitally varied their size to create an overlapping pattern of haptic replication. Some recede into the background, others rise to the surface, creating an overall sensation of floating upward and outward, an otherworldly irruption of the past into the present. In the images that flank it, tourist snapshots of the cemetery are montaged together in an almost abstract pattern; the actual subject of the photos can only be discerned on close inspection. The tinting of one red and the other green suggests either the demarcation of political bodies on either side of a border or the division between a bloody past and a verdant future. In an installation of the piece in 2011 at the Suzhou Creek Art Center in Shanghai, the three photographs were hung on the white wall of a gallery with a concrete floor and florescent lighting. A line of text ran the entire length of adjacent walls, to the left and right of the image, listing diplomatic details of Chinese-Vietnamese relations from 1950 to 2000, from alliance to conflict to normalization.
zh: 《子弹穿过年轻的心》（图7.04）是一组三联照片，每幅染成单色，并排悬挂时像一面炸裂国旗的色带。中央的黑白图像中，层层叠叠的墓碑挤满画面。麻栗坡的墓碑原本高度、形状统一，排列成笔直的队列，雷燕用数码手段改变其大小，制造出相互重叠、触感般的复制图案。有些退入背景，有些浮向表面，整体产生一种向上、向外漂浮的感觉，像是过去幽灵般闯入现在。两侧的图像把陵园的游客快照蒙太奇式拼成近乎抽象的图案，只有细看才能辨认照片的实际对象。一幅染红、一幅染绿，暗示着边界两侧政治身体的划界，或血染的过去与苍翠未来之间的分野。2011年，这件作品在上海苏州河艺术中心展出时，三幅照片挂在画廊白墙上，下面是水泥地面，头顶是荧光灯。一条文字沿两侧相邻墙壁的整个长度延伸，在图像左右列出1950年至2000年间中越关系的外交细节，从结盟、冲突到正常化。

Bullet Shot through a Young Heart

en: brings back to public consciousness the camouflaged history of loss in what is now often remembered only as a forgotten war. It serves as a meta-ideologizing return to a 1986 color print Lei Yan created after her deployment to the border.

(plate 17) depicts her longing for peace and for her young son from whom she was separated during her service. Although the woman at the battlefront reverses the gender positions in the classical lament of separation when a conscripted son leaves his mother, she has not been liberated from the sacrifice required by militarism. Only in sleep can the exhausted solider, arm and head draped over her medical supply kit, generate the glowing vision that staves off the black grid at her back. Against that abstraction—the entombing grate of a bunker, the emplotting matrix of history—her dream radiates outward in a ring of orange and red. The motif that encircles the soldier features a mythical mother clothed in the flowing robe of an immortal and surrounded by a flock of doves. She reaches for her child, serenades him, and finally holds him in her arms. Almost twenty years later, that dream returns, not in the guise of an idealized woman soldier whose service and sacrifice is justified by visions of peace, but in her challenge to the national diplomatic narrative by remembering the untold young lives the conflict laid waste to. It also marks Lei Yan’s position as an artist in southwestern China, with its historical and shifting economic and cultural relations with bordering Southeast Asian nations.
zh: 《子弹穿过年轻的心》把被伪装起来的丧失历史重新带回公共意识——这场战争如今往往只被记得为一场被遗忘的战争。它是一次元意识形态化的回归，回到雷燕驻守边境后于1986年创作的一幅彩色版画。《南疆之梦》（图版17）描绘她在服役期间与年幼儿子分离时对和平、对儿子的思念。尽管这位身处前线的女性颠倒了古典离别哀歌中应征入伍的儿子离开母亲时的性别位置，她并未从军国主义所要求的牺牲中获得解放。只有在睡梦中，这位疲惫的士兵——手臂和头伏在医疗包上——才能生出那团挡住背后黑色网格的辉光。在那片抽象——掩体的墓穴般格栅、历史的情节化矩阵——之前，她的梦以橙红色的光环向外辐射。环绕士兵的图案中，一位神话中的母亲身穿飘逸的仙人衣袍，周围是一群白鸽。她伸手去够自己的孩子，为他哼唱摇篮曲，最后把他抱在怀里。近二十年后，那个梦回来了，但不再是借理想化女兵的形象——她的服役与牺牲由和平幻象来辩护——而是借雷燕对国家外交叙事的挑战：她记住了那场冲突所摧毁的无数无名年轻生命。这也标明了雷燕作为中国西南艺术家的位置，那里与接壤的东南亚国家之间有着历史上的、不断变化的经济与文化关系。

en: Wang Nanming, the curator of Lei Yan’s 2011 solo show, has asserted that her work breaks through the marginalizing category of nüxing yishu because of its overt political engagement. In an attempt to revitalize this theoretical language, he coins the term

, translated as transfeminist art. He writes, “In trans-feminist art, women constitute a vital political power in the public sphere and are capable of discussing all sorts of issues of civic politics. Lei’s photograph series,

children: Bullet Shot through the Young Heart

en: , fights against the female identity superimposed upon female artists by Chinese modernity.”

Wang’s use of the prefix “trans” emphasizes crossing and questioning boundaries, public and private, male and female, East and West, and the ways these categories are mapped onto one another. It suggests how art by Chinese women moves across and into local and global debates about art and politics. It also implies a new category of art that supersedes gendered binaries and forms of power, demonstrating a progressive logic similar to that of postfeminism. This latter claim that feminism is over and done—that its demands for justice have already been achieved or actually hold women back, or that Western-style gender equity need only be exported to other, less enlightened parts of the world—willfully ignores ongoing and intersectional forms of social hierarchy.

Another understanding of Wang’s term of transfeminism emerges, however, if we consider that he arrives at it through his interpretation of work by He Chengyao and Lei Yan. The emphasis then shifts from overcoming feminism to thinking transhistorically across feminist movements, debates, and ruptures over the long twentieth century, in which women as a propositional category capable of shifting mass consciousness and as a collectivity of living social actors have since the beginning of Chinese modernity constituted “a vital political power in the public sphere.” The irony of the progressive-minded neologism authored by the male critic thus becomes its dependence on artists whose work is political not in spite of but because they are women who have focused a critical eye on the historical and political genealogies of gender that have caught and enabled them. It is through identification with and interrogation of subjects of Chinese modernity, the woman solider, military artist, and woman artist, that Lei Yan emerges as what Wang labels a transfeminist artist.
zh: 王南溟是雷燕2011年个展的策展人，他断言，由于雷燕作品中明显的政治介入，它突破了"女性艺术"这一边缘化范畴。为了复兴这套理论语言，他创造了"跨女性主义艺术"（kuanüxingzhuyi yishu）一词，英译为 transfeminist art。他写道："在跨女性主义艺术中，女性构成公共领域中一股重要的政治力量，能够讨论公民政治的各种问题。雷燕的摄影系列《子弹穿过年轻的心》，对抗中国现代性强加于女性艺术家的女性身份。"

王南溟使用前缀"跨"，强调穿越和质疑边界——公共与私人、男性与女性、东方与西方——以及这些范畴相互映射的方式。它暗示中国女性的艺术如何穿越并进入关于艺术与政治的本地和全球争论。它也意味着一种超越性别二元与权力形式的新艺术范畴，展现出与后女性主义相似的进步逻辑。后一种主张——女性主义已经结束，其正义要求已经实现，或实际上阻碍了女性，或者西方式的性别平等只需输出到世界上其他不那么开化的地方——刻意无视持续存在且相互交织的社会等级形式。

然而，如果我们注意到王南溟是通过对何成瑶和雷燕作品的解读得出这一术语的，那么对他所谓"跨女性主义"的另一种理解便浮现出来。此时重点不再是克服女性主义，而是跨历史地思考漫长二十世纪中的女性主义运动、争论与断裂；在这一视野中，女性作为能够推动群众意识的命题性范畴，也作为活生生的社会行动者的集体，自中国现代性肇始以来一直构成"公共领域中的一股重要政治力量"。于是，这位男性批评家所创的进步主义新词的讽刺之处，恰在于它依赖于这些艺术家——她们的作品之所以具有政治性，不是尽管她们是女性，而是因为她们是女性，而且她们把批判的目光投向性别的历史与政治谱系——这些谱系既束缚她们，也为她们提供行动的可能。正是通过认同并质询中国现代性的主体——女兵、军旅艺术家和女性艺术家——雷燕才成为王南溟所称的跨女性主义艺术家。

en: Arrested Ephemerality
zh: 被截停的短暂性

en: Lei Yan’s meditation on national, revolutionary iconography continued as she subjected objects from its corpus to material transmutation. Her works in ice, cloth, and paper capture the transience of image worlds. They arrest the process of disappearing, of being made ephemeral. They explore the contradiction between social idealism and social engineering. They evoke the volatile relationship between personhood and thingness, in which people can be treated as disposable, reproducible things, as much as things can be enchanted with humanity and life. In Arjun Appadurai’s conceit, “All things are congealed moments in a longer social trajectory.”

Lei’s experiments explore the social lives of things as congealed moments in a longer trajectory of cumulative history, in which revolutionary collectivity serves as the substrate for a politics of market desire and efficiency. Her return to her military past challenges the soft-glow feminization of revolution in the avant-garde guise of come-hither Red Guards (see figure 1.01) and the liberal subject often assumed in Western feminist thought and art. It connects past fields of disaster to those that persist in the present.
zh: 雷燕对国家革命图像学的沉思仍在继续，她让这套图像语汇中的物件经历物质转化。她的冰、布、纸作品捕捉图像世界的短暂性。它们截停了消失、被化为短暂之物的过程。它们探索社会理想主义与社会工程之间的矛盾。它们唤出人格与物性之间不稳定的关系：人可以像物一样被当作一次性、可复制的东西，物也可以被人性与生命赋魅。用阿尔君·阿帕杜莱的比喻来说，"一切事物都是更长社会轨迹中的凝结时刻。"
雷燕的实验探索物的社会生活，将它们视为更长累积历史轨迹中的凝结时刻；在这一轨迹中，革命集体性成为市场欲望与效率政治的基础。她对军旅过去的回归，挑战了先锋派表征中那种挑逗姿态的红卫兵式的、对革命的柔光女性化（见插图1.01），也挑战了西方女性主义思想与艺术中常预设的自由主义主体。它把过去的灾难场域与延续至今的灾难场域连接起来。

en: In 2006, Lei Yan created her

series. She froze personal military insignias—pins, badges, medals, a Red Guard armband, a folded military jacket, Mao’s little red book—in blocks of ice and photographed them. The images are titled according to the year of the preserved object, such as her Red Guard armband from 1969 or her
(eight-one) badge from 1985 after her Sino-Vietnamese War service.

The interplay between lighting and imperfections in the ice produces different effects. A red flag pin glows ethereally just under the slick surface of ice. A round badge falls into its depths, with Mao’s face on it blurred and opaque. The folded jacket of Lei’s dress uniform, with its distinctive lapels marking it as that of a woman soldier, lies shiny and stiff in encrusted ice. After photographing the frozen jacket in her studio, she transported the slab of ice to the edge of the city and erected it at the bottom of a slope covered in green foliage.

(plate 18), the photographic record of this ritual of mourning, documents a ghostly sentinel surrounded by leafy groundcover. It momentarily preserves and remembers the possibilities, the woman soldier and her talent development, as well as the losses, of life and revolutionary belief, as her tombstone melts into a forgotten landscape.
zh: 2006年，雷燕创作了《冰封的红色》系列。她把个人的军旅徽记——领花、像章、奖章、红卫兵袖标、叠好的军装、毛主席语录——冻在冰块里，然后拍摄下来。这些图像按被保存物品的年份命名，例如她1969年的红卫兵袖标，或1985年中越战争服役后的八一徽章。

光线与冰中瑕疵的相互作用产生不同效果。一枚红旗像章在光滑的冰面下发出空灵的光。一枚圆形像章沉入冰的深处，上面的毛泽东面孔模糊而不透明。雷燕军礼服的外套叠放着，其独特翻领表明这是一名女兵的军装，在结霜的冰中闪着光，僵直不动。在工作室拍完冰冻的军装后，她把那块冰运到城市边缘，竖立在一片绿荫覆盖的坡地底部。《无名之墓》（图版18）记录了这场哀悼仪式，拍下一名幽灵般的哨兵，周围是茂密的叶被。它短暂地保存并记住女兵及其才华发展的可能性，也记住生命与革命信念的失落，而她的墓碑正融入一片被遗忘的风景。

en: , Lei Yan froze old photographs of life on the Sino-Vietnamese front and then rephotographed them. The ice warps and fissures the original images: soldiers carrying supplies and loading tanks guns, the corner of a sandbag bunker, a dark hole in a white concrete structure with “tomb of nine female heroes” scrawled above it. In the thirty-six photographs of a series from 2007,
, Lei hones in on her own military career.

(figure 7.05), for example, features an ice-encased black-and-white photograph of the artist ten months after she joined the army. The face of the rifle-bearing teenage girl in uniform appears, through the refraction of light through ice, partly doubled. The unpredictability of the freezing process produces, by her own account, a remove from history that allows for observation of the past and consideration of it in relation to the contemporary moment, not unlike her binoculars in the

images. The crystalline clarity of ice reflects the purity of collective spirit and sacrifice that were strong ideological elements of her military training but also sealed her off from other ways of thinking.
zh: 在随后题为《子弹穿过年轻的心II》的系列中，雷燕把中越前线生活的老照片冻入冰中，然后重新拍摄。冰使原图像扭曲、开裂：背着补给、给坦克装弹的士兵；沙袋掩体的一角；白色混凝土结构中的一个黑洞，上方潦草地写着"九位女英雄之墓"。在2007年系列《冰封的青春》的三十六幅照片中，雷燕聚焦于自己的军旅生涯。例如《冰封的青春》第26号（图7.05）把艺术家入伍十个月后的一张黑白照片封在冰里。照片中，那个持枪、穿制服的少女，面孔透过冰的折射，出现部分重影。按她自己的说法，冻结过程不可预测，制造出一种与历史的距离，使她得以观察过去，并把它与当下联系起来，就像她在《如果》图像中举起的望远镜。冰晶般的清澈映照着集体精神与牺牲的纯粹——这些是她军事训练中强大的意识形态元素，但也把她与其他思考方式隔绝开来。

en: Lei Yan’s use of old photos in these two series followed a 1990s trend examined by Wu Hung in “The ‘Old Photo Craze’ and Contemporary Chinese Art.” The low-budget, mass-produced serial
(Old photos), launched in 1996, gave its readers a platform to publish everyday photographs accompanied by written reflections. Wu argues that
served as a vehicle for “constructing a different type of history—history as collage and chance result, and as the synthetic voice of a multitude of amateur authors.”

In turning to the use of old photos by Chinese contemporary artists, he identifies three approaches: works that represent memories of major, often suppressed historical events such as the Cultural Revolution; works that construct ordinary, personal histories; and works in which photos appear as “ruins” reflecting the instability of historical memory.
Lei Yan’s
employs all three of these approaches at once.

The series assembles an ordinary, personal history of participation in suppressed historical events meant to produce collective identification, including the Cultural Revolution and the Sino-Vietnamese War.
It preserves these forgotten memories in a way that captures the magnifying and obscuring effects of the preservation process. It seizes on the multivalent visual idexicality of old photos.
zh: 雷燕在这两个系列中使用老照片，呼应了巫鸿在《"老照片热"与当代中国艺术》中考察的1990年代潮流。1996年创刊的低成本、大众化系列读物《老照片》，为读者提供了发表日常照片并附文字感想的平台。巫鸿认为，《老照片》是"建构另一种历史——作为拼贴与偶然结果的历史，作为众多业余作者合成声音的历史"的载体。
在考察中国当代艺术家使用老照片的方式时，他辨认出三种路径：表现对重大、往往遭压抑的历史事件（如文化大革命）之记忆的作品；建构普通个人历史的作品；以及照片作为"废墟"出现、反映历史记忆之不稳定性的作品。
雷燕的《冰封的青春》同时采用了这三种路径。
该系列汇集了一部普通的个人史，其中参与的是那些旨在制造集体认同、却遭压抑的历史事件，包括文化大革命和中越战争。
它保存这些被遗忘的记忆，同时捕捉保存过程本身的放大与遮蔽效应。它抓住了老照片多价的视觉指示性。

en: Moving on to the medium of cloth, Lei Yan created a series of soft sculptures titled

(figure 7.06), which grew out of her obsession with the material she wore for thirty years as a soldier. While camouflage ostensibly provides cover and protection for military personnel on the battlefield, it also produces a uniform, national body to which other forms of identification are subordinated. Lei likens its patterning to the mixed, patchwork identities of those such as herself who have lived through multiple political movements in China. The fabric is also a global commodity entangled in the hierarchical, gendered relations of outsourced labor and related political battles over whether national military uniforms should be produced overseas.

Lei’s sculptures crafted out of camouflage include daily-use items, such as kettles, teacups, cooking utensils, vases, sewing machines, telephones, and laptop computers. The gleaming utilitarian surface of industrially produced objects, which in the model kitchen turned battlefield once signified Cold War narratives of surpassing the enemy, now appear handmade, floppy, and rumpled. As readymade replicas cut from a textile developed for combat, they parody the symbolic myth-making power of things.
zh: 转向布这一媒介，雷燕创作了一系列题为《迷彩生产》的软雕塑（图7.06），其源于她对她作为士兵穿了三十年的材料的迷恋。迷彩表面上为战场上的军人提供掩蔽与保护，同时也生产出一种统一的、国家的身体，其他形式的认同都从属于它。雷燕把迷彩图案比作像她这样经历过中国多场政治运动者混杂、拼贴式的身份。这种面料也是一种全球商品，纠缠于外包劳动的等级化、性别化关系，以及关于国家军服是否应在海外生产的政治争斗。
雷燕用迷彩制作的雕塑包括日用品，如水壶、茶杯、炊具、花瓶、缝纫机、电话和笔记本电脑。工业化生产物品那光亮的实用表面——在样板厨房变成战场的年代，它曾意味着超越敌人的冷战叙事——如今显得手工、松软而皱巴。作为用为战斗开发的纺织品裁出的现成品复制品，它们戏仿了物的象征神话制造力。

, 2007. Fabric sculpture. Courtesy of the artist.

children: 图7.06　雷燕，《迷彩生产》，2007年，织物雕塑。艺术家提供。

en: Lei Yan’s reference to domestic space and use of needlework resonate with works often included in a global canon of feminist art, such as the
project that Judy Chicago hoped to re-create with Chinese interlocutors, but Lei injects these now familiar tropes with the Chinese history of woman soldier/art soldier. In
, camouflage items cover gallery walls in a random, almost haphazard way.

This installation amasses and scatters across white walls the signs of household containment and geopolitical conflict; frenzied materialism and national sacrifice; domestic and global economies. Its chaotic arrangement suggests the dual frontlines the modern Chinese woman has faced: the double duty of political and domestic labor. Tasked with both symbolic representation of the nation and sociobiological reproduction of the family, she has been mobilized and demobilized, pulled into public production and returned to the kitchen, according to the needs of the state.

At the catachrestic conjunction of woman soldier/art soldier/woman artist, Lei Yan confronts the double bind of either serving the nation, regardless of its repressions, or being stuck in “inner quarters” of domestic introspection. The enthusiastically titled
, which spoofs patriotic love of country and the idea of domestic bliss, stitches together public and private, as domains that are not dichotomous but differentially constructed through each other.
zh: 雷燕对家庭空间的指涉和对针线活的使用，与全球女性主义艺术经典中常收录的作品产生共鸣，例如朱迪·芝加哥希望与中国对话者一起重建的"女人屋"计划；但雷燕为这些如今已为人熟知的意象注入了女兵／艺术战士的中国历史。在《我爱厨房》中，迷彩物品以随意、近乎杂乱的方式覆盖画廊墙面。
这件装置把家庭禁锢与地缘冲突的符号、狂热的物质主义与国家牺牲、家庭经济与全球经济，积聚并散布在白墙之上。其混乱布置暗示中国现代女性面临的双重前线：政治劳动与家务劳动的双重职责。她既被要求承担国家的象征表征，又承担家庭的社会生物学再生产，于是随着国家需要被动员、被复员，被拉入公共生产，又被送回厨房。
在女兵／艺术战士／女性艺术家这一词语误用式的交汇处，雷燕直面双重束缚：要么服务于国家，不论其压迫；要么困于家庭内省的内闱。那个热情洋溢的标题《我爱厨房》戏仿了对国家的爱国之爱与家庭幸福生活的观念，把公共与私人缝合在一起，视为并非二分、而是通过彼此差异化建构的领域。

children: A Place Where Dream Starts, No. 6

children: 图7.07　雷燕，《梦开始的地方》第6号，2011年，纸与线软雕塑。艺术家提供。

en: After ice and cloth, Lei Yan began sculpting objects out of paper, producing ghostlike facsimiles that evoke the absent human presence of those who once wore or carried these things. Her 2011 series,

(figure 7.07), consists of objects from everyday military life: cap, sneakers, artillery belt, cups, canteen, and handheld missiles. Fashioned after the things she once had an intimate material relationship with, they are reminiscent of traditional Chinese funerary offerings, paper objects burned to accompany the dead into the afterworld. The dream implied by the title and the ethereal quality of the spot-lit sculptures suggest the reveries of youth and idealism. Their light, crumpled paper surfaces take recognizable shape and simultaneously make it appear insubstantial. The dream then becomes one of redemption for those lost to past worldings and the work of art that set up those worlds and made them visible, tangible, desirable, material.
zh: 在冰与布之后，雷燕开始用纸塑造物件，制作出幽灵般的仿制品，唤起曾经穿戴或携带这些东西的人不在场的存在。她2011年的系列《梦开始的地方》（图7.07）由军旅日常生活中的物品组成：帽子、运动鞋、炮兵腰带、杯子、水壶和手持导弹。这些仿照她曾与之有亲密物质关系的物品做成，让人联想到中国传统丧葬明器——为陪伴死者进入来世而焚烧的纸物。标题所暗示的梦，与聚光灯下雕塑的空灵质感，暗示着青春与理想主义的遐想。它们轻薄、皱褶的纸面呈现可辨认的形状，同时又显得虚幻不实。于是梦变成一种救赎之梦，既为那些失落于过往世界营造的人，也为艺术曾经承担的工作——建立那些世界，使它们可见、可触、可欲，并具有物质实在。

en: This meta-ideological meditation on her military past emerged from a piece Lei Yan created two year prior. The question of its title

? (figure 7.08) is posed to the children who died en masse in the 8.0-magnitude earthquake that hit the Sichuan counties of Wenchuan and Beichuan on May 12, 2008. Shoddy construction of classrooms and dormitories amplified the natural disaster’s death toll. Collapsed school buildings crushed and killed thousands of students, many of whose bodies were never recovered. Their grieving parents declared the engineering of the buildings, some recently constructed, not just tofu but tofu dregs. Those who demanded a count of the number of student deaths and investigation into corrupt officials and contractors who had taken shortcuts were silenced in the name of stability. From this landscape of disaster, official media broadcast a story of humanitarian aid and the reestablishment of “harmonious society” after an exceptional event.

Social critics attempted to peel back the veneer of this picture and the loss it obscured. The Wen-chuan earthquake, like other social crises and controversies, became a touchstone for artists negotiating a new market-driven valuation of art, its traffic in images, and a legacy of aesthetic commitment to social commentary and collective political struggle. Ai Weiwei, for example, responded to the student deaths with projects that blended the creation of modernist art objects on a spectacular scale with online social activism, performative confrontations with Chinese police and legal systems, and documentary filmmaking. While the international place of prominence given to Ai’s activities has tended to eclipse other work, he was one among many artists moved by this and related scenes of chronic disaster amid an everyday landscape of environmental degradation and economic inequality.
zh: 这场对她军旅过去的元意识形态沉思，源自雷燕两年前创作的一件作品。其标题《我如何保护你？》（图7.08）中的问题，是向2008年5月12日四川汶川、北川8.0级地震中成群罹难的孩子提出的。教室与宿舍的劣质建筑放大了自然灾害的死亡人数。倒塌的校舍压死数千名学生，许多人遗体始终未能找到。悲痛欲绝的家长宣称，这些建筑——有些还是新近建成的——不只是豆腐，而是豆腐渣。那些要求统计学生死亡人数、调查偷工减料的腐败官员与承包商的人，被以稳定之名噤声。官方媒体从这片灾难景观中播出的，是一个人道主义救援的故事，以及在非常事件之后重建"和谐社会"的故事。

社会批评者试图剥开这幅画面的表皮，揭示它所遮蔽的丧失。汶川地震像其他社会危机与争议一样，成为艺术家们处理的试金石，涉及艺术在市场驱动下的新估值、图像的流通，以及美学上致力于社会批判与集体政治斗争的遗产。例如，艾未未以多种项目回应学生之死，把壮观尺度的现代主义艺术物品创作，与网络社会行动、与中国警察和法律系统对抗的行为表演，以及纪录片制作结合起来。尽管艾未未的活动所获得的国际显要位置往往遮蔽了其他作品，他只是在环境退化与经济不平等的日常景观中，被这幕及类似慢性灾难场景所触动的众多艺术家之一。

en: From a distance, Lei’s installation of

? looks like a pile of trash. On closer inspection, it becomes apparent that she has meticulously re-created the site of a collapsed school building. Working with translucent white filter paper, needle, and thread, she sculpted crumpled walls, pillars, and furniture. Small details buried within pull viewers closer, implicating them as voyeuristic witnesses to a crime scene. Shoes, pencil boxes, and backpacks spill out from the rubble. Small black-and-white student photographs are tucked into the front pockets of the backpacks (figure 7.09). Tiny paper flowers on long, weedy stems sprout from the scattered personal effects. For the parents of children whose bodies were never recovered, these objects remained all they could collect. Some assembled possessions pulled from the rubble together with stuffed animals, snacks, and bottled drinks to builds altars to their disappeared children in front of school ruins. These ritual offerings, which inverted the Chinese practice of ancestor worship, with a parent feeding the memory of a child instead of the other way around, insisted on the existence of lost lives the state tried to erase with money offered for families’ silence. Lei Yan’s hand-sewn re-creation of everyday use objects reenchants them in a similar way, while her choice of materials echoes the condemnatory criticism of poorly constructed buildings as tofu dregs. These ghost objects, rather than easing spiritual passage like their ritual counterpart of joss paper burned in veneration of the dead, stand in instead for life after life in a field of death and disaster, where the unequal distribution of life and death are justified by the intertwined projects of late socialism and late liberalism. The paper sculpture series that followed include
and

, a cluster of bags and suitcases arranged on the cement floor of an empty factory space. Together these three-dimensional explorations in the flimsy medium of paper evoke the precariousness of life—the ubiquitous traffic between personhood and thingness—for the young soldier, the migrant worker, the lost child, those unaccounted for and gone missing again and again.
zh: 从远处看，雷燕的装置《我如何保护你？》像一堆垃圾。靠近观察，才会发现她一丝不苟地重建了一栋倒塌校舍的现场。她用半透明的白色滤纸、针和线，塑造出皱褶的墙壁、柱子和家具。埋在其中的细小细节把观者拉近，使他们成为犯罪现场的窥视证人。鞋子、铅笔盒和书包从瓦砾中溢出。小小的黑白学生照塞在书包前袋里（图7.09）。细长、杂草般的茎上开着纸花，从散落的私人物品中钻出。对于遗体始终未能找到的孩子的父母来说，这些物品仍是他们所能收集的一切。有些家长把从瓦砾中找出的物品与毛绒玩具、零食、瓶装饮料摆在一起，在校舍废墟前为他们失踪的孩子搭建祭坛。这些仪式供品颠倒了中国祖先崇拜的实践，变成父母喂养对孩子的记忆，而不是反过来；它们坚持那些被国家试图用封口费抹除的逝去生命的存在。雷燕对手缝日常用物的再创造，以类似方式使它们重新赋魅；而她选择的材料，呼应了把劣质建筑斥为豆腐渣的谴责性批评。这些幽灵般的物件不像其仪式对应物——为敬奉死者而焚烧的纸钱——那样帮助灵魂过渡，而是代表死亡与灾难场域中一个生命又一个生命的存在；在那里，生与死的不平等分配，由晚期社会主义与晚期自由主义相互交织的工程所辩护。随后的纸雕系列包括《梦开始的地方》和《在路上》——一组袋子和手提箱，摆在一处空置厂房的水泥地上。这些以轻薄纸张为媒介的三维探索，共同唤出生命的不稳定性——人格与物性之间无处不在的流转——为年轻士兵、民工、失去的孩子，为那些一次又一次下落不明、消失无踪的人。

children: 图7.08、7.09　雷燕，《我如何保护你？》，2011年，纸雕，展览现场及局部。艺术家提供。

en: Monumental Ephemeral
zh: 纪念碑式／短暂性

en: At the turn of the millennium, a new culture industry took up contemporary art as a way to advance China’s national image on the global stage. The state enlisted the names and talents of “dissident” figures who had spent years abroad or whose work had once been censored. Artists like Ai Weiwei and Cai Guoqiang and filmmakers like Zhang Yimou and Jia Zhangke contributed to the monumental spectacles of the 2008 Beijing Olympics and 2010 Shanghai World Expo. These twenty-first-century spectacles of awe-inspiring national achievement continued a legacy of form that runs through imperial and Maoist China: of artworks, buildings, and rituals executed on a grand scale. Large-scale structures from the Great Wall to the Monument to the People’s Heroes in Tiananmen Square to the Bird’s Nest Stadium are invested with the power of monumentality, the control and shaping of collective memory. As Wu Hung notes in an essay on the subject, “The Latin root of monumentality means recalling and admonishing. In order to exercise the function of admonition, official monuments always are awesome, majestic, and inhuman structures; their huge mass controls the public space in which they are placed.”

As a challenge to this function, Chinese avant-garde artists in the 1980s and 1990s experimented with antimonumentality, creating pieces that Wu identifies as either countermonuments or attempts to achieve antimonuments. Hence, the large number of experimental art projects on the Great Wall. The problem with an antimonumental critique of monumental power is that it often slides toward that which it aims to deconstruct. The propensity of Chinese experimental artists to make large-scale pieces that command the world’s attention perpetuates the socialist mandate to forge a new political order through cultural production and revolution. This like-sized response to the hegemony of art as state politics and to the global cultural order of things risks mimicking and reproducing the spectacular society it purports to critique. It engages in a politics of scale that continues to
in powerful ways.
zh: 世纪之交，一种新的文化产业把当代艺术当作在全球舞台上推进中国国家形象的方式。国家征用了那些曾在海外多年、或作品曾被审查的"异见"人物的名字与才华。艾未未、蔡国强等艺术家，张艺谋、贾樟柯等电影人，参与了2008年北京奥运会和2010年上海世博会这些纪念碑式的盛景。这些21世纪令人惊叹的国家成就景观，延续了一种贯穿帝制中国与毛泽东时代中国的形式遗产：以宏大尺度创作艺术品、建筑与仪式。从长城到天安门广场的人民英雄纪念碑，再到鸟巢体育场，大型结构都被赋予了纪念碑性的力量，即对集体记忆的控制与塑造。正如巫鸿在一篇相关论文中所说："纪念碑性（monumentality）的拉丁词根意为回忆与告诫。为了行使告诫功能，官方纪念碑总是令人敬畏、庄严、非人的结构；其巨大的体量控制着它所置身的公共空间。"

作为对这种功能的挑战，1980年代和1990年代的中国先锋艺术家实验反纪念碑性，创作出巫鸿所说的反纪念碑，或试图达成非纪念碑的作品。因此才有大量以长城为题的实验艺术计划。对纪念碑式权力进行反纪念碑批判，问题在于它常常滑向它想要解构的东西。中国实验艺术家偏爱创作吸引世界注意的大型作品，这延续了社会主义的使命：通过文化生产与革命锻造新的政治秩序。这种以同等尺度回应艺术作为国家政治的霸权，以及全球文化物序，可能模仿并再生产它声称批判的景观社会。它参与一种尺度政治，并继续以强大的方式从事世界营造。

en: Ai Weiwei, who gained local and global distinction through his role as design consultant on the National Stadium for the Beijing Olympics, serves as the most prominent example of this phenomenon, as well as the contradictions that arose during this turning-point period for Chinese contemporary art. Even in his later critique of the Olympics, antagonism to the state, and commitment to art as social activism, his activities assumed an epic scale: in their formal aesthetics, resources commanded for their realization, and international recognition for their bad boy political dissent. In William Callahan’s analysis of Ai as a figure of ironic tensions, he observes the mutual dependence of dissidents and officials for “their respective legitimacies and identities,” in which “Ai’s anti-state oppositional discourse thus tends to reproduce the state even as it resists it.”

The pieces Ai Weiwei created in response to the Wenchuan earthquake, exhibited in museums around the world, are monumental in scale. They admonish state silence, even as they represent that same nation-state in the international art arena.
zh: 艾未未因担任北京奥运会国家体育场设计顾问而获得本地与全球声誉，是这一现象最突出的例子，也是中国当代艺术这一转折时期出现的矛盾的例子。即便在他后来对奥运会的批判、对国家的对抗，以及把艺术当作社会行动的承诺中，他的活动也呈现出史诗般的尺度：形式美学、为实现作品所调动的资源，以及因其坏男孩式的政治异见而获得的国际认可，皆如此。在威廉·卡拉汉把艾未未分析为反讽张力人物的文章中，他观察到异见者与官员"各自合法性与身份"的相互依赖："艾未未反国家的对抗话语因此往往在抵抗国家的同时再生产国家。"
艾未未为回应汶川地震而创作、在世界各地博物馆展出的作品，在尺度上是纪念碑式的。它们谴责国家的沉默，同时又在国际艺术舞台上表征同一个民族国家。

en: In Lei Yan’s
?, paper sculptures of backpacks spill out from insubstantial, ghostly rubble. In Ai Weiwei’s

, installed in 2009 across the façade of Munich’s Haus der Kunst, nine thousand colorful children’s backpacks write out in bubbly Chinese characters, “She lived happily in this world for seven years.” A Beichuan mother who refused compensation money for her daughter’s death wrote this sentence as what she wanted people to remember. For

, an installation piece first exhibited in his 2012–13 survey show at the Hirshhorn Museum in Washington DC, Ai purchased thirty-eight tons of mangled rebar salvaged from the earthquake reconstruction zone and hired a team of workers to hammer it straight. He then arranged it in piles of various heights to create a long, rolling landscape of rusted steel ruptured by fault lines. The accompanying wall text read, “The tragic reality of today is reflected in the true plight of our spiritual existence. We are spineless and cannot stand straight.”

(2008–11) records the name, gender, age, school, and class of 5,212 children who perished in the earthquake, information collected by the hundreds of citizen volunteers who responded to Ai Weiwei’s online call for an investigation into the student deaths. Installed at the Hirshhorn, the list spanned a massive, curving wall. A monument to the dead and the collective labor it took to document them, it resembles a war memorial. Lei Yan’s small rumpled paper sculpture

, created in 2012, also presents a list. Three flower-strewn tablets record crises of the millennium’s first decade with the Wenchuan earthquake inserted into a transnational field of death and injury in combat zones, terrorist actions, industrial accidents, and natural disasters.
zh: 在雷燕的《我如何保护你？》中，背包的纸雕从不坚实的、幽灵般的瓦砾中溢出。在艾未未的《铭记》中，九千个彩色儿童书包于2009年铺满慕尼黑艺术之家的立面，用圆润的中文字体写出："她在这个世界上幸福地生活了七年。"一位北川母亲拒绝为女儿之死接受赔偿金，她写下这句话，作为她希望人们记住的内容。在《直》中——这件装置作品首次展出于华盛顿赫希洪博物馆2012—13年艾未未回顾展——艾未未购买了从地震重建区回收的三十八吨扭曲钢筋，雇了一队工人把它锤直，然后将其堆成高低不一的垛，构成一片被断层线撕裂的锈蚀钢地景。展墙上的说明文字写道："今日的悲剧现实，映照出我们精神存在的真实困境。我们毫无脊梁，无法站直。"《四川名单》（2008—11）记录了5212名在地震中罹难儿童的名字、性别、年龄、学校和班级；这些信息由数百名公民志愿者收集，他们响应艾未未的网上呼吁，要求调查学生死亡。安装在赫希洪博物馆时，名单铺满一整面巨大的弧形墙。它是一座献给死者的纪念碑，也是记录他们所付出的集体劳动的纪念碑，形似战争纪念碑。雷燕2012年创作的小型皱纸雕塑《早逝的十年》也呈现了一份名单。三块散布着花朵的碑板记录了新千年第一个十年的危机，把汶川地震插入一个跨国死亡与伤痛场域——战区、恐怖行动、工业事故与自然灾害。

en: It would be facile in comparing these works—the monumental and the ephemeral—to reinscribe familiar dichotomies of male/female, liumang/nüxing, public and private. Such a normativizing move would erase the traces of the ephemeral in the monumental and of the monumental in the ephemeral. Considering art by Ai Weiwei and Lei Yan together, while a seeming “impossible reality” in current curatorial rules of the game, makes it possible to see them also as ethnographic fragments of avant-garde/xianfeng cultural transition. As much as Lei Yan’s work inhabits an image world of late Qing and early Republican illustrations of women with binoculars to their eyes, so too is it in relationship with pieces like Ai Weiwei’s
, and

. Holding these works together is a way of understanding Chinese contemporary art in the expanded field, putting those marginalized by globalized, professionalized circuits back in and asking what new questions and lines of sight this method of montage opens up. How does a feminist lens highlight the contradictions of an emerging art world and enable a differential consciousness about the shifting role of art—as ideological, institutional, and imaginative—within various configurations of power?
zh: 比较这两类作品——纪念碑式的与短暂性的——时，若只是重新刻写男／女、流氓／女性、公共／私人这些熟悉的二分法，便流于肤浅。这种规范化举动会抹去纪念碑中的短暂性痕迹，以及短暂性中的纪念碑性痕迹。把艾未未与雷燕的艺术放在一起考虑，尽管在现行策展游戏规则中看似"不可能的现实"，却使我们得以把它们也视为avant-garde／先锋文化转型的民族志碎片。正如雷燕的作品栖居于晚清民初举望远镜女子的图像世界，它也与艾未未的《铭记》《直》《四川名单》等作品发生关系。把这些作品放在一起，是在扩展场域中理解中国当代艺术的一种方式：把被全球化、专业化循环边缘化的人重新放回去，并追问这种蒙太奇方法开启了什么新问题与新视线。女性主义镜头如何凸显一个新兴艺术世界的矛盾，并使人们形成一种差异意识，去理解艺术——作为意识形态的、制度的与想象的——在各种权力配置中不断变化的角色？

en: The biographies of these two artists, born within months of each other in the early years of the People’s Republic, read in parallel reveal shifts and struggles among what Bourdieau identifies as the fields of cultural production, of power, and of economics or class relations.
Ai Weiwei was born in 1957. His father—a poet who had studied in France, endured Guomindang imprisonment, joined Mao at Yan’an, and edited

—was denounced that same year in the Anti-Rightist Campaign and sent to China’s northwest with his family. After seventeen years of exile in Heilongjiang and Xinjiang, they returned to Beijing. In 1978, Ai Weiwei briefly attended the Beijing Film Academy. A red princeling, heir to a patriline of art and politics, vagrancy and imprisonment, he left China for the United States in 1981. For twelve years he lived in New York, where he studied at the Parsons School of Design, befriended Allen Ginsberg, and became a peripatetic photographer of East Village life. Lei Yan was also born in 1957, into the family of a career officer in the People’s Liberation Army. She followed her father into the military, studied printmaking as part of her army training, photographed life on the Sino-Vietnamese front, and received advance training at the pla’s Arts Academy. When Ai Weiwei became the official Chinese consultant to the Swiss firm designing the Beijing Olympics National Stadium, it seemed like the ultimate

(outside-the-system) artist had reversed position in service to a monumental statement of China’s arrival on the world stage. When Lei Yan posed “what if” questions to Mao retrospectively adorned with a 1930s female hairstyle, it seemed like the ultimate
(inside-the-system) artist had reversed position in a deconstructive tour of the past and its archives.
zh: 这两位艺术家都生于中华人民共和国成立后的早期岁月，出生时间相隔数月；并置阅读他们的传记，可以揭示布尔迪厄所说的文化生产场域、权力场域以及经济或阶级关系场域之间的转变与斗争。

艾未未1957年出生。他的父亲是一位诗人，曾留学法国，经历国民党监禁，赴延安追随毛泽东，后来主编《人民文学》；就在同一年，他在反右运动中被批判，和家人一起被送往中国西北。在黑龙江和新疆流放十七年后，他们回到北京。1978年，艾未未曾短暂就读于北京电影学院。作为一个红色太子党——继承着艺术与政治、漂泊与监禁的父系血脉——他于1981年离开中国前往美国。在纽约生活的十二年间，他在帕森斯设计学院学习，与艾伦·金斯伯格成为朋友，成为东村生活的游走摄影师。雷燕也生于1957年，出身于中国人民解放军职业军官家庭。她追随父亲进入军队，在部队训练中学习版画，在中越前线拍摄生活，并在解放军艺术学院接受高级培训。当艾未未成为瑞士公司设计北京奥运会国家体育场的官方中方顾问时，那个看似最彻底的"体制外"艺术家仿佛转变了立场，为一个宣告中国登上世界舞台的纪念碑式作品服务。当雷燕以1930年代女性发型追溯性地装扮毛泽东，并提出"如果"问题时，那个看似最彻底的"体制内"艺术家仿佛转变了立场，展开了一场穿越过去及其档案的解构之旅。

en: Their unfolding lives and works, shaped by a history in which art and politics were never understood as autonomous realms, briefly approach each other in their responses to Chinese state image management of the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake. Are they part of the same or competing sectors of the field of cultural production? Their reversals in relation to the “system,” as well as the depth of their conceptual practices and aesthetic excavations, force a reworking of Bourdieu’s analytic framework, which was developed in a bourgeois European context. Art in the Maoist field was theorized as aligned with revolutionary power, rather than in a dominated or inverted relationship with it. It did not tend toward the dominant pole of the field of capitalist class relations; its superstructure was intended to lead the base, to smash colonial and class hierarchy. Chinese contemporary art in the era of late socialism–late liberalism is a field of contradictory historical and ideological forces and of competing institutionalized authorities and economies. This has become the playing field for an artist like Ai Weiwei, imprisoned and embraced by the monumentalizing gestures of canonization. His art commands public museum spaces the world over, exposing (and solidifying) the Chinese state in the name of freedom and progress. The work of Lei Yan, a former pla propagandist working from the edge of the nation and the margins of the international art world, raises the following questions: What spectres of “always already absent present” haunt Ai Weiwei’s aesthetic experiments?

For whom are these heroic politics of exposure most persuasive? What makes London’s Tate Modern broadcast from its rooftop the message “Release Ai Weiwei,” rather than “Recognize and compensate the families of lost children” or “The people have suffered from the coalition of government and business”?
zh: 他们展开的生命与作品，由一段艺术与政治从未被理解为自主领域的历史所塑造；在回应中国国家对2008年汶川地震的图像管理时，二者短暂地彼此接近。他们属于文化生产场域中相同的部分，还是相互竞争的部分？他们相对于"体制"的反转，以及他们观念实践的深度与美学挖掘，迫使人们重做布尔迪厄的分析框架——该框架是在欧洲资产阶级语境中发展起来的。在毛泽东时代的场域中，艺术被理论化为与革命权力结盟，而不是与它处于被支配或颠倒的关系。它并不趋向资本主义阶级关系场域的主导极；它的上层建筑意在引领基础，粉碎殖民与阶级等级。晚期社会主义—晚期自由主义时代的中国当代艺术，是一个充满矛盾的历史与意识形态力量、相互竞争的建制化权威与经济的场域。这里已成为像艾未未这样的艺术家的竞技场；他既被经典化过程中的纪念碑化姿态所禁锢，也被其接纳。他的艺术占据全世界公共博物馆空间，以自由与进步之名暴露（并巩固）中国国家。雷燕的作品出自一名前解放军宣传干部之手，她从民族国家的边缘与国际艺术界的边缘工作，提出以下问题：什么样的"总是已经缺席的在场"的幽灵萦绕着艾未未的美学实验？
这些英雄式的暴露政治对谁最有说服力？又是什么让伦敦泰特现代美术馆从屋顶发出"释放艾未未"的信息，而不是"承认并赔偿失去孩子的家庭"或"人民饱受政府与商业联盟之苦"？

en: In June 1994, five years after the events of June 4, Ai Weiwei photographed his wife, the artist Lu Qing, in Tiananmen Square. She stands in front of the Gate of Heavenly Peace, her back against the pedestrian barricade on the opposite side of Chang’an Boulevard, far away enough that her head appears next to and the same size as Mao’s in the larger-than-life portrait that hangs behind her. Her head cocked to the side and one foot propped up on the metal barricade, she stares casually at the camera while lifting her translucent black skirt with both hands to expose her underwear. In a twist on the socialist use of the female body to expose and attack class enemies, her flippant pin-up pose disregards and diminishes the monumental power of Mao. Although the photograph has since circulated as an early example of Ai Weiwei in “Fuck Off” mode, at the moment of its initial exposure, the question of artistic agency remains open to speculation. Is Ai Weiwei as photographer or Lu Qing as performer the artist? Who is the image made for? A year later Ai Weiwei stood further from the Gate in Tiananmen Square and photographed his own hand flipping a middle finger to Mao’s portrait. In

, his raised digit in the foreground takes the place of Lu Qing’s body next to the Chairman, looming large beside the portrait, threatening to blot it out. The woman and her conflicted, embodied politics of exposure disappear from the picture. Almost two decades later, Ai Weiwei created a large-scale piece for the 2013 Venice Biennale titled

. Its six parts—Supper, Accused, Cleansing, Ritual, Entropy, Doubt—depict in realist detail his eighty-one day prison detention in 2011. Large iron boxes, installed in the place of pews in a church turned art gallery, contain half-scale plexiglass dioramas of the incarcerated artist being interrogated, showering, eating, shitting, and sleeping. Spectators can observe these scenes through small glass windows on the sides or tops of the boxes. In a sculptural installation that takes on the weight and scale of history painting, the artist’s own body on display becomes the locus of indignity, suffering, and resistance. It is a spectacular form of self-portraiture haunted by a Maoist legacy of charismatic male leadership.
zh: 1994年6月，即6月4日事件五年后，艾未未在天安门广场拍摄了他的妻子、艺术家路青。她站在天安门前，背靠长安街对面的行人护栏，距离足够远，使她的头出现在身后那幅巨型毛泽东画像旁边，且大小相同。她歪着头，一只脚搭在金属护栏上，随意地盯着镜头，同时用双手撩起半透明的黑裙，露出内裤。这是对社会主义利用女性身体来揭露和攻击阶级敌人的一次反转：她轻佻的招贴女郎姿态无视并缩小了毛泽东的纪念碑式权力。尽管这张照片后来作为艾未未"滚蛋"（Fuck Off）模式的早期例子流传，但在它最初曝光之时，艺术能动性的归属仍有待探究。作为摄影师的艾未未，还是作为表演者的路青，才是艺术家？这张图像是为谁而作？一年后，艾未未站得更远，在天安门广场拍摄自己向毛泽东画像竖中指的手。在《透视研究》中，前景里他竖起的手指取代了路青在主席旁边的身体，在画像旁赫然耸立，几乎要将其遮蔽。女人及其充满冲突的、具身的暴露政治从画面中消失了。近二十年后，艾未未为2013年威尼斯双年展创作了一件大型作品《S.A.C.R.E.D.》。它的六个部分——《晚餐》《被告》《清洗》《仪式》《熵》《怀疑》——以写实细节描绘他2011年被监禁的八十一天。大型铁箱安装在由教堂改成的美术馆里，取代了长椅，里面装着半比例的有机玻璃立体模型，再现这位被囚艺术家受审、洗澡、进食、排便和睡觉的场景。观众可以通过铁箱侧面或顶部的小玻璃窗观察这些场景。在这件具有历史画重量与尺度的雕塑装置中，艺术家自己的身体成为屈辱、受难与抵抗的展示场所。这是一种奇观式的自画像，被毛泽东时代富有魅力的男性领导遗产所萦绕。

en: Lei Yan’s paper sculptures are similarly haunted but respond to the legacy by a refusal to authoritatively represent. Her arrested objects resist the temporal pull of narrative and modernity’s myth of progress. Their empty presence decenters the human subject, drawing attention instead to absences and omissions in normative stories of art, feminism, and nation. Her lightweight sculptures turn away from the tradition of history painting so central to socialist aesthetics and toward the genre of the still life. An evacuated pair of military sneakers was one of the first forms she fashioned out of paper. They give shape to what Norman Bryson analyzes in still life painting as the voiding of individual or idealized human presence: “Still life takes on the exploration of what ‘importance’ tramples underfoot.”

Jacques Derrida likewise ruminates on the relationship between subject and object through a still life painting of shoes: “As soon as these abandoned shoes no longer have any strict relationship with a subject borne or bearing/wearing, they become the anonymous, lightened, voided support (but so much the heavier from being abandoned to its opaque inertia) of an absent subject whose name returns to haunt the open form.”
zh: 雷燕的纸雕塑同样被萦绕，但它回应这份遗产的方式是拒绝权威性再现。她被截停的物件抵抗叙事的时间牵引与现代化的进步神话。它们空无的在场使人类主体去中心化，转而把注意力引向规范性的艺术、女性主义与民族故事中的缺席与遗漏。她轻巧的雕塑背离社会主义美学中如此核心的历史画传统，转向静物画。一双被掏空的军旅运动鞋，是她最早用纸塑造的形态之一。它们赋予诺曼·布列逊在静物画分析中所说的个体或理想化人类在场之清空以形状："静物画承担了对'重要性'所践踏之物的探索。"
雅克·德里达同样通过一幅鞋子静物画来思考主体与客体的关系："一旦这些被遗弃的鞋子不再与任何被承载或承载／穿着它们的主体保持严格关系，它们就成为一个缺席主体之匿名、轻盈、被清空的支撑（但因为被遗弃于其不透明的惰性中而沉重得多），这个主体的名字回来萦绕这开放的形式。"

en: The Hallowed Object
zh: 神圣之物

en: Lei Yan has continued to work in paper, manipulating, creasing, and sewing the flat material into a surfeit of three-dimensional objects, each of which would readily fit in the hand. For

, a 2016 solo exhibition in Beijing’s Caochangdi art district, she displayed seventy-six sculpted objects en masse, arranged along a narrow shelf the entire length of a gallery wall. The exhibit also included black-and-white photographs of the objects—some taking representational shape, others uncanny in form—as single pieces or in small groupings. A tall, slender cone topped with a five-point star stands forlornly on its own. An upright axe and sickle turn away from each other. A larger assembly of objects (figure 7.10) resembles a domestic still life with bottles, vases, and a candlestick, but it also includes the axe and sickle, a bugle, an antitank missile, and a trench mortar bomb nose down and fins in the air. What might seem to be an ornamental vessel with a handle turns out to be a hand grenade. Eccentrically shaped containers mingle with those of recognizable use. In the long three-dimensional display along the wall, the accumulated abundance of objects becomes a procession, a tableau vivant, even a cityscape. Overproduction, whether of symbolic imagery or industrial goods, is hallowed and hollow. The wrinkled, white shapes vacillate between solid and void. The Chinese title for the series,

, can also be translated as relic. The reliquary Lei Yan has created, however, does not produce reverence for or the aura of an individual hero. They invoke reflection on cast-off ideals of collectivity and on who or what endures.
zh: 雷燕继续用纸创作，通过摆弄、压折和缝纫，把扁平材料变成大量三维物品，每一件都能握在手中。在2016年北京草场地艺术区个展《神圣之物》中，她集中展示了七十六件雕塑物品，沿着一面画廊墙全长的窄搁板排列。展览还包括这些物品的黑白照片——有些呈现具象形状，有些形态诡谲——单件或小组合呈现。一只高而细的圆锥顶端顶着五角星，孤零零地立着。一把竖立的斧头与镰刀彼此背对。一组更大的物品（图7.10）像是一幅家庭静物，有瓶子、花瓶和烛台，但其中也包括斧头与镰刀、一把军号、一枚反坦克导弹，以及一枚弹头朝下、尾翼朝上的迫击炮弹。一个看似带把手的装饰性容器，其实是手榴弹。奇形怪状的容器与用途可辨的容器混杂在一起。在沿墙的长长三维展示中，积聚的丰富物品变成队列、活人画，甚至城市景观。过度生产——无论是象征图像还是工业产品——既神圣又空洞。皱褶的白色形体在实体与虚空之间摇摆。该系列的中文标题"圣物"，也可以译为 relic（遗物）。然而雷燕创造的这件圣物匣，并不生产对个体英雄的崇敬或灵光。它们引发对集体性这一被丢弃理想的反思，以及对谁或什么得以持存的反思。
